summary: Iteration 6 frontend retest of the device-handoff banner fix in Player.jsx (wasActiveHereRef gate). RESULT: ALL CRITERIA PASS ✅. The 'playback-moved-banner' and 'resume-here-btn' are NEVER present/visible across the entire flow (first open of station A, Back, Edit A + Update Station, reopen A, Back, open station B, Back, reopen A — 4 player opens total). Crash regression from iteration_4/5 remains FIXED: 0 webpack overlays, 0 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)' errors / pageerrors across the full flow. player-container + spotify-player-container render on every open. POST /api/spotify/tracks fires exactly 4 times (one per station open). Back-to-Stations (pause-on-leave effect) works without console/page errors. Only pageerror observed is the expected harmless 'No supported keysystem was found.' (EME/DRM) — same as last iteration.
critical_code_review_comments: Player.jsx is now ~811 lines — still recommended to split into PlayerCore / Visualizer / BumperManager / DeviceHandoff modules for maintainability.

Polling log 'Polling: No state available' still fires every 1s indefinitely without a Premium device — high console noise. Consider stopping the poller after N consecutive nulls to reduce noise in dev/automation.

resumePlaybackHere() can still silently fail if deviceIdRef.current is null and spotifyPlayerRef.current.resume() is unavailable. Since the banner is now correctly gated by wasActiveHereRef this is much less likely in practice, but consider disabling the resume-here-btn until deviceIdRef.current is set as a belt-and-braces guard.

wasActiveHereRef is initialized to false on every Player mount; if a real user navigates away (Back) and the SDK had been active, on return the ref resets and the banner won't show even if Spotify has moved playback off this device. Acceptable trade-off given the persistent player layer (Player isn't unmounted on Back), but worth verifying behaviour holds for real Premium users since the Player layer is kept mounted in App.js (so the ref survives across Back/forward — good).
test_credentials: Auto-auth via ?spotify_auth=success — stored Spotify token auto-refreshes (no Premium device in headless, so SDK never reaches isActive=true; this is exactly why the wasActiveHereRef gate works in automation).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Banner false-positive bug is FIXED and crash regression remains FIXED. The wasActiveHereRef gate on line ~671-676 of Player.jsx correctly prevents the banner during SDK handshake / headless automation. Persistent Player layer in App.js (player-layer div with display:none toggle, not unmount) means wasActiveHereRef survives Back/forward navigation — important for real Premium UX. Note that this also means SDK is only initialized once (sdk_inits=1 in iteration_5 evidence; in this run we saw 0 SDK 'device ready' callbacks because the SDK never reached ready state in headless, which is fine and consistent with banner staying hidden). For future iterations: if Spotify Premium-device behaviour ever needs to be verified end-to-end, this must be done with a real device — not possible in this automation harness.

verification_evidence.A-open: player-container=present, spotify-player-container=present, banner_visible=False, resume_btn_visible=False, len_errs=0, tracks_posts=1
verification_evidence.Back-to-stations-1: banner_visible=False, len_errs=0, no pageerror from pause-on-leave
pageerrors: No supported keysystem was found. (expected EME/DRM)

rca_of_the_issue: Previous iteration_5 bug was due to unconditional `if (state.isActive === false) setPlaybackMovedAway(true)` in the react-spotify-web-playback callback, which fires during SDK handshake and continuously in environments without a Premium device. Fix verified in iteration_6: a wasActiveHereRef useRef(false) is set to true only when state.isActive===true, and the banner is set only when state.isActive===false AND wasActiveHereRef.current === true. In headless automation the SDK never reaches isActive=true, so the ref stays false and the banner correctly never appears — matching the intended UX of 'banner only when playback was actually active here and then moved elsewhere'.
